body.value: Knowledge that evolves. Responsible practice. Human commitment.

The National Association for Psychotherapy, Family Therapy and Coaching (ANTHEC) is a Moroccan association connecting psychological wellbeing, professional development and service to individuals and families. We bring knowledge into practice, encourage continuing education and cooperation, and promote ethics that respect people and professional boundaries.
People and quality practice at the heart of our work
Awareness grows when knowledge is accessible, and practice improves through learning, exchange and accountability. We seek to connect practitioners, researchers, institutions and communities.
Our areas of action
Training and professional development: meetings, workshops and programmes to deepen practitioners’ knowledge and develop their tools.
Family and community: awareness, prevention and initiatives supporting family relationships and access to appropriate help.
Research and shared experience: scientific dialogue, discussion of practice and knowledge development.
Cooperation and partnerships: joint projects extending the reach of initiatives to the people concerned.
Your place in the association

Whether you are a professional, a student or interested in psychological wellbeing and community action, explore the membership pathway that suits you. Applications are reviewed and approved under the conditions of each category.
Stay informed
Find announced activities, participation conditions and association updates through our programme and news pages.

pages.title: About us
pages.search_description: ANTHEC is an independent Moroccan association with scientific, professional and humanitarian aims. Its statutes state that it was founded on 20 March 2025.

body.value: A professional and human framework for psychological wellbeing
ANTHEC is an independent Moroccan association with scientific, professional and humanitarian aims. Its statutes state that it was founded on 20 March 2025. Its head office is in Agdal, Rabat.

The association connects quality professional practice with community needs. Its areas include psychotherapy, family therapy, family counselling and mediation, coaching, training, research and related support and rehabilitation fields, respecting the qualifications and boundaries of each speciality.
Why was the association founded?

We seek a space where practitioners can pursue continuing learning, ethics and cooperation while making psychological awareness accessible to individuals and families. The association aims to reduce stigma, encourage appropriate help-seeking and support initiatives suited to Moroccan society.
How we work

Interdisciplinary exchange, training, scientific discussion, field initiatives and partnerships support our goals. We value clear roles, beneficiaries’ dignity and a connection between competence and accountability.
A national identity open to cooperation
The statutes provide for branches and centres and cooperation within Morocco and abroad. Structures, partnerships and programmes that are actually approved are announced through official channels.

pages.title: Vision, mission and values
pages.search_description: A society where psychological wellbeing is part of everyday awareness, individuals and families receive support that respects their dignity, and practition

body.value: Our vision

A society where psychological wellbeing is part of everyday awareness, individuals and families receive support that respects their dignity, and practitioners develop their skills within a responsible professional culture.
Our mission

Contribute to psychotherapy, family therapy and coaching in Morocco through continuing education, shared experience, research, community awareness and partnerships, grounded in ethics and respect for professional boundaries.
Values that guide us
Human dignity: respect each person, their experience and privacy, without discrimination.
Professional responsibility: practise within competence, recognise limitations and refer to an appropriate specialist when needed.
Knowledge and learning: remain open to scientific discussion, review tools and develop skills.
Integrity and clarity: explain activities, membership and accreditation accurately, without exaggerated promises.
Independence: preserve independent association decisions within its rules and aims.
Cooperation: develop complementary relationships between professionals, researchers, institutions and community actors.
Community service: respond to individuals’ and families’ needs, with attention to vulnerable groups.

pages.title: Our goals
pages.search_description: Our goals connect support for practitioners, knowledge development, awareness and cooperation. They guide programme choices according to available resource

body.value: Professional development and community service
Our goals connect support for practitioners, knowledge development, awareness and cooperation. They guide programme choices according to available resources and approved priorities.
Develop practice and competence
Contribute to the association’s fields, provide continuing education and professional exchange, support practitioners’ tools and pathways, and strengthen ethics and respect for specialities.
Promote awareness and prevention
Build a culture of psychological wellbeing, reduce stigma around seeking help, encourage prevention and family communication, and support children, adolescents, families and vulnerable groups.
Encourage research and knowledge
Support studies, scientific meetings, shared experience and publications that help understand community needs and improve practice.
Support initiatives and cooperation
Support relevant projects and partnerships with institutions, universities, training centres and associations, exchanging experience nationally and internationally.
Contribute to professional dialogue
Responsibly represent practitioners’ concerns and contribute to institutional discussions about the field and quality of practice, within the association’s role and applicable laws.

pages.title: Areas of work
pages.search_description: We encourage cooperation across disciplines while respecting training, competence and intervention boundaries, and distinguishing therapy, counselling, reh

body.value: Complementary specialities, clear roles
We encourage cooperation across disciplines while respecting training, competence and intervention boundaries, and distinguishing therapy, counselling, rehabilitation and coaching roles.
Psychotherapy and psychological counselling
Scientific and professional exchange on psychological approaches, skills development, quality practice, ethics and appropriate guidance for beneficiaries.
Family and couples therapy, family mediation
Family relationships, communication, marital and educational challenges: encouraging approaches that respect everyone’s rights and each family’s circumstances.
Coaching and personal and professional development
Goal setting, skills, decision-making and career development within a clearly defined intervention, with referral when needs exceed the practitioner’s competence.
School and educational support
Awareness and support around learning, communication and educational relationships, in cooperation with families, educators and relevant partners.
Rehabilitation and related non-medical disciplines
The statutes mention natural and physical therapy, speech therapy and psychomotor therapy. Cooperation rests on complementary roles, referral and the qualifications specific to each field.
Cross-disciplinary areas
Training, research, prevention, awareness, community action, partnerships and support for professional initiatives.

body.value: From shared knowledge to action
Our programmes combine scientific meetings, practical learning and community awareness. Each activity announces its topic, audience, facilitators, date, format and participation conditions.
Scientific and professional meetings
Conferences, discussions and round tables on psychotherapy, family therapy and coaching, encouraging interdisciplinary exchange.
Case studies and shared experience

Meetings on practice, hypothesis formulation and intervention choices use anonymised cases and exclude identifying details. Each announcement specifies whether the meeting is educational or supervisory.
Workshops and continuing education
Thematic programmes combining theory and practical exercises, with entry requirements, learning outcomes and the type of certificate where one is offered.
Awareness and field initiatives
Talks, workshops, campaigns and programmes for families, students, educators and relevant groups, according to each initiative and available partnerships.
Explore activities
Upcoming activities: discover announced programmes. Past activities: read the reports and resources published by the association.

body.value: Continuing learning for evolving practice
Continuing education and shared experience are professional priorities. Programmes help participants deepen knowledge, understand tools and their limits, and connect learning to practical situations.
What do programmes include?

Talks, practical workshops, case studies and experience-sharing meetings may be offered. The format depends on the topic and audience; each programme specifies entry level, aims and participation conditions.
Choose a suitable programme
Before registering, review the content, facilitators’ published qualifications, target audience, duration, format, any fees, and the document issued after participation and its requirements.
Clear certificates and outcomes

Each programme states whether it offers a participation, attendance or other specified certificate. A certificate must be understood within the programme’s scope; it does not by itself change a participant’s professional status or competence.
For professional members
Participation opportunities, benefits and discounts are announced for each programme. Conditions may vary by membership category, capacity and activity.

pages.search_description: Through awareness, prevention and community initiatives, we support psychological wellbeing and family relationships. We offer accessible knowledge that re

body.value: Awareness close to individuals and families

Through awareness, prevention and community initiatives, we support psychological wellbeing and family relationships. We offer accessible knowledge that respects people’s experience and distinguishes general guidance from the need for specialist help.
Areas of interest
Family relationships: communication, marital challenges, family roles and parenting.
Children and adolescents: psychological and educational needs, encouraging cooperation between family, school and professionals.
Prevention and reducing stigma: responsible dialogue about psychological wellbeing and seeking help.
Vulnerability and crises: initial support and referral initiatives with competent organisations, according to available resources and announced programmes.
How to take part
Find initiatives open to the public in the activities section. For programme information or initial guidance, contact the association; we will explain the available service and how to access it.
Each initiative states its dates, fees or free access, and eligible audiences. Membership does not automatically provide therapy sessions or individual services.

body.value: Research and knowledge
We encourage questioning, analysis and shared knowledge across our fields. We aim to support studies and scientific discussion addressing professional practice and Moroccan society’s needs.
This may include research meetings, scientific contributions, critical readings, field studies and research partnerships under projects approved and announced by the association.
Resources and publications
Find articles, summaries, information materials and guides published by the association. Contributions credit their authors and sources and include dates, respecting copyright and personal privacy.
Educational resources support understanding; they do not replace individual assessment by a qualified professional when needed.
News and updates
Follow official announcements, registrations, meetings, approved partnerships and activity reports. Updates are dated and programme status is clearly stated to help readers find accurate information.

pages.title: Association governance
pages.search_description: The statutes define the association’s bodies and responsibilities. Governance distributes roles, coordinates bodies and oversees programmes and administrat

body.value: Clear responsibilities and institutional working
The statutes define the association’s bodies and responsibilities. Governance distributes roles, coordinates bodies and oversees programmes and administrative and financial management.
National general assembly
The highest decision-making body considers directions and reports and decides matters under the powers, meeting and voting rules set out in the statutes.
Founding council

The statutes define its membership and role, following the national general assembly in the order of bodies. It supports strategic follow-up, implementation and coordination within its responsibilities.
National executive board and presidency

The board manages association affairs and follows programmes and relationships. The president coordinates and represents the association under the statutes, with administrative, financial and other duties distributed within the board.
Services, committees and branches
The statutes allow their creation under defined rules. Only structures actually established with approved information are presented, explaining their responsibilities and scope.
Officers and founding members
Approved names and roles appear in the directory below. Founding and institutional status are distinct from professional membership levels and accreditation.

pages.title: Join the association
pages.search_description: We welcome people interested in our aims, practitioners, students and people working in our fields. Membership categories provide suitable pathways, subjec

body.value: Learning, responsibility and participation
We welcome people interested in our aims, practitioners, students and people working in our fields. Membership categories provide suitable pathways, subject to application review and approval.
Categories and annual fees
Member: 100 MAD. For people interested in psychological wellbeing, community action and the association’s aims.
Affiliated member: 500 MAD. A professional pathway requiring review of training, experience and supporting documents.
Advanced member: 1,500 MAD. Professional participation and learning under the category’s conditions and announced programmes.
Accredited member: 3,000 MAD. The association’s highest professional membership level, subject to application acceptance and accreditation conditions.
Founding and honorary members: fee exemption according to approved status. This status cannot be obtained simply by selecting it or making a payment.
From application to membership

Create an account, complete your profile, select a category and attach required documents. Administration reviews the application and requests any additional information. Follow its payment instructions; membership begins after administrative confirmation.
Validity and renewal

Annual membership lasts one year from administrative confirmation. Early renewal preserves remaining validity; late renewal starts from the new approval date. Founding and honorary statuses follow their specific rules.
Before applying
Read the statutes, approved rules and ethical charter. Each category specifies its benefits; membership does not guarantee accreditation approval or a place in every programme.

pages.title: Professional and programme accreditation
pages.search_description: The association grants accreditation under its criteria and procedures. Each document identifies its scope, beneficiary, reference, validity and status so

body.value: Accreditation with a defined scope
The association grants accreditation under its criteria and procedures. Each document identifies its scope, beneficiary, reference, validity and status so it can be understood and verified.
Professional accreditation

This is linked to the accredited member level. Approval or renewal triggers the grant or renewal of professional accreditation, with a gold card and a separate certificate under approved conditions. Professional accreditation lasts one year.
Other membership documents confirm membership status and category; they do not themselves confer third-level professional accreditation.
Course or training programme accreditation

A separate application may be made and reviewed. Accreditation, if granted, covers the named programme and its approved duration only, without automatic extension to other programmes or the organiser’s activities.
Meaning and limitations

Accreditation represents an association decision within the scope stated. It is not a government licence and does not replace requirements for practising any profession. A training attendance certificate does not automatically become professional accreditation.
Applications and enquiries
Contact administration for the procedure, documents and review conditions. Detailed programme accreditation fees are communicated privately during application processing.

pages.title: Ethical charter
pages.search_description: Our charter places respect for the person and their interests at the centre of professional relationships. Members commit to competence, clarity and integr

body.value: Trust begins with responsible practice

Our charter places respect for the person and their interests at the centre of professional relationships. Members commit to competence, clarity and integrity, respecting privacy and professional boundaries.
Professional principles
Dignity and non-discrimination: respectful and fair treatment across backgrounds, circumstances and beliefs.
Beneficiaries’ interests: avoid harm and exploitation, and match interventions to needs and practitioner competence.
Competence and learning: update knowledge and tools, and seek supervision or professional consultation when needed.
Scope of competence: explain the intervention and refer when needs exceed training or competence.
Confidentiality: protect professional information and explain the limits and obligations applicable in context.
Honesty and transparency: explain services, limitations and conditions, avoiding misleading claims and exaggerated promises.
Integrity of relationships: avoid exploitation and relationships compromising responsibility or the beneficiary’s interests.
Respect for colleagues: encourage cooperation and responsible discussion without defamation or abuse.
Accountability

Concerns and alleged breaches are reviewed within the association’s remit and rules, respecting privacy and the parties’ rights. Publicly posting complaints does not replace their formal handling process.

pages.title: Partnerships, cooperation and volunteering

body.value: Partnerships built on shared aims
We seek cooperation with institutions, universities, research and training centres, associations and community organisations to support psychological wellbeing, families and skills development.
Areas of cooperation

Awareness, prevention, scientific meetings, continuing education, research, field initiatives and support for families, students and relevant groups. Each project defines its scope, responsibilities and implementation conditions.
Our partners
Only partnerships approved for publication are shown. Their nature is explained; publishing a name or logo does not endorse every activity or service of that organisation.
Propose a partnership

Introduce your organisation and work, explain the proposed cooperation, audience and contribution, and provide contact details. Administration reviews the proposal and may request information; submission does not constitute approval.
Volunteering and contributions

Interested people may propose knowledge, organisational or communication contributions. Proposals are reviewed according to programme needs and skills, with tasks and responsibilities clarified before participation.
Specialist tasks are assigned to suitably qualified people. Open volunteering opportunities and their conditions are announced when available.

pages.title: Document verification
pages.search_description: Check its status using the document’s QR code or by entering its reference and additional verification code.

body.value: Verify an association document
Check its status using the document’s QR code or by entering its reference and additional verification code.
What does the result show?

The information needed to verify the document: name, document type, reference, validity period and status. There is no public name search or access to the member’s file, photograph or private information.
Read the status before relying on a document
A document may be valid, expired, suspended or cancelled according to the current register. A printed copy or image cannot establish its current status after issue; check the result on the website.
If no result appears
Check the reference and code or use the original QR link. If the problem persists, contact administration with the reference, without publishing the private code.
Earlier test documents are not official documents; launching the website does not make them official.

pages.title: Frequently asked questions
pages.search_description: Yes. The member category welcomes people interested in our aims. Professional levels require application review and their specific conditions.

body.value: Can I join without being a professional?
Yes. The member category welcomes people interested in our aims. Professional levels require application review and their specific conditions.
Does creating an account mean acceptance?
No. The account allows application submission and tracking. Membership starts after the required steps and administrative confirmation.
Is payment sufficient for acceptance?
Acceptance depends on application review and meeting the conditions. Follow administration’s instructions about when to pay and how to provide evidence.
How do I choose a professional level?
Review category conditions and provide accurate training and experience information. Administration may request additional documents and clarify the suitable level under approved criteria.
Is every professional member accredited?
No. Professional accreditation is linked to accredited member status. Another membership-level document does not replace it.
How long are membership and accreditation valid?
Annual membership and professional accreditation last one year according to the approved confirmation date. Course accreditation covers the programme’s approved duration.
Are all activities free for members?
Benefits and fees vary by category and activity. Each programme explains free access or discounts, eligibility and booking conditions.
Is accreditation a government licence?
It is association accreditation within its stated scope and does not replace the legal requirements of any profession.
How do I correct my information or an issued document?

Update the fields available in your account and contact administration regarding issued documents. Profile changes do not automatically alter older documents; correction may require a recorded reissue.
Can I pay by bank card on the website?
The current process records and administratively reviews payments according to association instructions. It does not include an integrated online payment gateway.
Can a minor apply for membership?
Processing requires the legal representative’s consent under the approved procedure. Contact administration for the appropriate requirements.
